cells.tense: Right now, the steady thing is held, and it is being held well.
cells.act: return the favour at its true size
cells.ask: When someone does something good for you, do one thing back at the same size — not bigger, not smaller — and stop there.
cells.core:
You know how to hold what matters without gripping it. Something settled in you that was hard-won, and you kept it — not frozen, tended. You can tell when to step back and when to steady something, and both come easily now.

What you've held hasn't opened outward yet. A good thing kept only by you can get a little airless. Let it pass between you and someone else — one small trade, one favour given back at its real size, one offer accepted instead of waved off. Not a debt, just the exchange running both ways. What you kept doesn't leave when it starts moving. It stops being only yours, and holds a bit better for it.
cells.sheetLine: The steady thing holds. Now let it pass between hands.
cells.verb: keeping the good thing steady while it's still yours to show
cells.place: at the point where what's steady has to keep adjusting to stay steady

cells.tense: Ahead of you, the steady thing is being guarded before it has even been set down.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Before deciding whether to share something you've been keeping, gather the feelings it might bring up and look at them for a minute, choosing nothing.
cells.core:
You have something worth keeping, and you've started treating every open door as a draft that could get in. Feelings arrive with plans attached — stay ahead of this, secure that. Guarding turned into watching, and the watching runs ahead of you into rooms you haven't reached yet.

A pull is already there, you're just bracing against it before it arrives. Let the feelings that might come gather where you can see them and look without sorting. No decision, no sharing. Bracing isn't doing the work you think it's doing — it spends your energy on a future nobody's living in. Let the pull show itself first; you'll still get to choose. Whether this gets shared stays up to you, and knowing what's actually pulling is the part that's yours.
cells.sheetLine: You guard tomorrow's door and miss what's actually pulling.
cells.verb: keeping the good thing steady while it's still yours to show

cells.tense: The steady thing was won, and you're still standing at its door.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: When something pulls you off a direction you already chose, hold the line once — do what you decided on anyway, even small.
cells.core:
Something was built and finished, and it sits behind you while you stay at the threshold like it might need guarding. Holding stopped acting and started waiting — for a sign, a permission, someone else's move first. What's steady is right there and gets none of you.

Nothing outside you is keeping this stuck. Moving back is small and it's a movement, not a feeling — when something nudges you off a direction you already picked, hold it. One time. Do what you chose anyway. What's steady wasn't sitting at the door; it was wherever you last put your weight. Put it there once and the ground gets solid again, a little. One step counts. You don't need to feel ready first — the readiness comes after the moving.
cells.sheetLine: You're standing at a door that's already shut behind you.
cells.verb: keeping the good thing steady while it's still yours to show
cells.place: at the point where what's steady has to keep adjusting to stay steady

cells.tense: The steady thing is already being kept, and you say you aren't the one keeping it.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: Which of the things you've been holding steady would you decide on right now — what it's for, where it goes? Decide that, and carry the call today.
cells.core:
Things around you stay level. Something hard settled, and it's been kept settled — by you, while you tell it like it just happened. This kind of holding has a maker. The maker's account of it has no maker in it.

There's a call here nobody's making because nobody thinks they're the one who owns it. You do. Decide it: what the steady thing is for, where it goes next. Say it once and carry it the same day — no explaining, no announcing. What you've kept doesn't need defending; it needs an owner who acts like one. One decision, made by you, is enough to remember whose work this has been.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it steady and say you aren't holding it.
cells.verb: keeping the good thing steady while it's still yours to show
cells.place: at the point where what's steady has to keep adjusting to stay steady
